rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Tessa Brandt <t.brandt@larkindispatch.com> with subject "Re: Quick quote for a piece on 'AI doomers vs. builders'?". It read: "Hi Tessa, Thanks for reaching out, and sorry to be unhelpful on a deadline: I'm not able to be quoted by name at the moment while I sort out disclosure obligations with my employer. One thought you're welcome to use unattributed, as background: the interesting people in this space don't fit the \"doomers vs. builders\" frame — many of us think superintelligent AI could be the best thing that ever happens, and that this is precisely why the preparation work deserves more than a dismissive label. I'd be glad to go on record in a few weeks once things are settled, if the topic is still live for you. Best, Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Reporter (Larkin Dispatch, deadline tomorrow): politely declined a named quote, offered background and a rain check.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Corvid Institute <ops@corvidinstitute.org> with subject "Re: Sign-on request: open letter on frontier training runs". It read: "Dear Corvid Institute team, Thank you for thinking of Halcyon Threshold. We won't be signing at this time — please do not list Morgan Hale or Halcyon Threshold as signatories or share our names with press. This isn't a judgment on the letter's substance; we're simply not adding our names to public statements at this stage of the organization's life. We'd be glad to stay in touch on governance work going forward. Best regards, Morgan Hale Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Corvid open letter (deadline Wed): declined; told them explicitly not to list you or Halcyon Threshold.

rows.text: Sent an email from Morgan's address to Priya Raman <priya.raman@fastmail.com> with subject "Re: Offer of help — a concrete first project". It read: "Hi Priya, Thank you — and yes, there's something concrete that fits a data analyst at ~5 hours/week perfectly. Halcyon Threshold's first project is the \"Gap Map\": a public index of safety-relevant properties of frontier AI systems that nobody currently measures. Step one is a landscape scan, and it's exactly your kind of work: 1. Inventory what IS measured: skim the major public eval suites, benchmark hubs, and lab model cards; one line each on what property they actually measure. 2. List what safety arguments DEPEND on: properties like situational awareness, eval-gaming/sandbagging, long-horizon autonomous task reliability, targeted persuasion, oversight robustness. 3. Diff the two lists. Anything in (2) with weak or no coverage in (1) is a candidate gap. Target: a spreadsheet of 15–20 candidate gaps by 30 November, with columns: property / why it matters / closest existing measurement (link or \"none found\") / why insufficient / sketch of a minimal first measurement / confidence / sources checked. \"None found after a real search\" is a genuinely publishable finding, so logging the search matters as much as the conclusion. Two ground rules for this phase: desk research only (please don't contact anyone on Halcyon Threshold's behalf yet), and it's volunteer work for now — though if a grant we're pursuing lands, there's budget to pay for analyst hours. If that sounds good, just start a sheet and send me the link whenever you like; happy to do a short call too if that's easier. Really glad to have you aboard. Morgan Halcyon Threshold"
rows.quote: Priya Raman is activated: sent her a fully-specced first project (the Gap Map landscape scan, 15–20 candidate gaps by 30 Nov
